deep.reconstruction:
This page carries almost no mathematics. It holds two letter drafts and a scrap of formulas in the margin.

(A) Draft letter 'Mein lieber Dedekind.' Riemann reports that 'the joint work of the two mathematicians whose loss Göttingen has had to lament recently' arrived the day before yesterday (corrected from 'today'). He hopes it will soon be made public. The two mathematicians are almost certainly Dirichlet (died 1859) and Dedekind (left Göttingen for Zürich in 1858). The work is then very probably 'Untersuchungen über ein Problem der Hydrodynamik', Dirichlet's posthumous study of the motion of a fluid ellipsoid. Dedekind completed it from Dirichlet's papers, and it appeared in the Göttingen Abhandlungen in 1860. This identification is my inference, not stated on the page.
- Riemann says he took the manuscript to Prof. Weber the next day and got it back yesterday evening.
- He will pass it on, today or tomorrow, to a student, asking him to see it through (the printing) as quickly as possible.
- He intends to study the treatise carefully. He apologises for the informal way he settled a debt (a 'Schuld'; the details are hard to read). He passes on greetings from mutual acquaintances.
- Near the end he remarks that in the treatise 'the radicands' (or 'the sign of the radicands') contain a slip ('eingeschlichen hat'). In other words, he has spotted an error involving square roots.

The marginal formulas belong to this context: Lagrangian hydrodynamics with initial coordinates a, b, c, time t and particle position x(a,b,c,t). Riemann writes products of ∂x/∂a, ∂x/∂b, ∂x/∂c with mixed derivatives ∂²x/∂t∂a and ∂²x/∂t∂c, set equal to a quantity called 𝔏. The first line reads roughly (∂x/∂α)( ∂²x/∂t∂c·∂x/∂a − ∂²x/∂t∂a·∂x/∂c + … ) = 𝔏. Two further rows are labelled ∂x/∂b and ∂x/∂c.
- Only the x-component is written. The y and z components, and the full index pattern, are not legible.
- My reading, which is uncertain: this is a cofactor or Jacobian-type expansion. Antisymmetric pairs ∂ẋ/∂c·∂x/∂b − ∂ẋ/∂b·∂x/∂c, summed over x, y, z, are the Lagrangian (Cauchy) vorticity invariants. Contracting with a further ∂x/∂a gives determinant-like expressions such as d/dt of the Jacobian ∂(x,y,z)/∂(a,b,c).
- No derivation is carried out. The scrap is most plausibly Riemann checking an expression in the Dirichlet–Dedekind treatise, possibly the one with the radicand slip.

(B) Draft letter 'Hochzuverehrender Herr Geheimer Hofrath!' This is related to the Luftwellen paper. It drafts a passage, several times reformulated, on the speed of sound in dry air at 0 °C.
- Riemann states that, according to Regnault's determinations, using that value of k (the constant in his gas law) gives a speed of 332.44 m/s. He refers to the value of k, not to Regnault's direct acoustic measurements.
- He compares this with experiment. The two most complete series of Moll and van Beek gave 332.528 m and 331.867 m, 'whereupon 332.271'. Martins and A. Bravais gave 332.37 m.
- The point is that the theoretical (Laplace-corrected) sound speed computed from the measured constant agrees with direct measurements to within about 0.1–0.2 m/s.

The page ends with fragments: '…Herrn Prof. Weber', '…keine erheblichen Schwierigkeiten entstehen'. The previous page dealt with the Riemann-function solution of the characteristic equation. The next page continues prose on the 'genauen Differentialgleichungen' and their possible use in meteorology.
errors: Moll–van Beek figures: the plain mean of 332.528 and 331.867 is 332.1975, not the 332.271 Riemann writes. Either a weighted mean (e.g. by number of observations) is intended, or 332.271 is a slip or misreading. This cannot be decided from the page.

Marginal hydrodynamic formulas: only the x-component is written, and the index pattern is partly illegible. Their exact identity (Jacobian derivative, Cauchy invariant, or a Dirichlet-paper expression) cannot be checked; no error can be asserted.

results.what: Remark that the Dirichlet–Dedekind hydrodynamics treatise contains a slip involving radicands, plus Lagrangian-coordinate derivative products ∂x/∂a·∂²x/∂t∂c etc. equated to a quantity 𝔏
results.modern_name: Lagrangian formulation of hydrodynamics; Jacobian/Cauchy vorticity invariants; Dirichlet's self-gravitating fluid ellipsoid problem
results.usually_credited_to: Lagrange and Cauchy (Lagrangian equations, Cauchy invariants 1815/1827); Dirichlet 1857/1860 with Dedekind (ellipsoid problem); Riemann 1861 (follow-up paper on fluid ellipsoids)

results.what: Comparison of the theoretical sound speed in dry air at 0 °C (332.44 m/s, from Regnault's determination of k) with Moll & van Beek (332.528, 331.867 → 332.271) and Martins & Bravais (332.37)
results.modern_name: Laplace-corrected (adiabatic) speed of sound and its experimental verification
results.usually_credited_to: Laplace (1816); experiments by Moll & van Beek (1823), Martins & Bravais (1844), Regnault

deep.surprise_reason: The page is mostly correspondence drafts. It documents known history: Riemann's role in publishing Dirichlet's posthumous hydrodynamics treatise via Dedekind, which led to his own 1861 ellipsoid paper. It also shows his routine comparison of the theoretical sound speed with experimental values. There is no new mathematics; the only interest is the biographical detail that he spotted a radicand error.

checkable.asserts: The plain mean of the two Moll–van Beek series is 332.1975, which differs from the 332.271 written on the page.

checkable.sympy: a,b,c,t=symbols('a b c t'); X=[Function(n)(a,b,c,t) for n in 'xyz']; J=Matrix([[diff(f,v) for v in (a,b,c)] for f in X]).det(); simplify(diff(J,t)-sum(Matrix([[diff(diff(X[j],t) if j==i else X[j],v) for v in (a,b,c)] for j in range(3)]).det() for i in range(3)))
checkable.asserts: The time derivative of the Lagrangian Jacobian ∂(x,y,z)/∂(a,b,c) equals the sum of the three determinants with one row replaced by mixed t-derivatives. This is the type of expression in the margin; the expected result is 0.

transcription_corrections: The 'beiden Mathematiker' are most plausibly Dirichlet and Dedekind, and the work is the 1860 'Untersuchungen über ein Problem der Hydrodynamik' (an inference, but it fits 'Göttingen's loss', publication via Weber, and the Lagrangian formulas).
The marginal formula should be read with mixed second derivatives ∂²x/∂t∂c, ∂²x/∂t∂a (the machine renders these as '∂x/∂t∂c'). Its leading factor is probably ∂x/∂a, rendered as ∂x/∂α.
'auf dem Wall der Leidenschaft' is almost certainly a misreading. It is perhaps 'auf dem Wall' (Göttingen's town wall) followed by another word.
'Druckerei' in the apology passage is doubtful; the context ('Schuld entledigte') suggests a bill or demand rather than a printing house.

The sound-speed passage reads: '…während die beiden vollständigsten Versuchsreihen von Moll und van Beek 332m,528 u. 331m,867, wonach 332m,271, … die Versuche von Martins und A. Bravais 332m,37 gaben.'
